title: Understanding the Bootstrap Distribution
text: The bootstrap distribution is used to estimate the variability of a statistic by resampling with replacement from the original data. In this case, it helps us understand the variability of the difference in sample means, \( \bar{K}-\bar{D} \).

title: Interpreting the Null Hypothesis
text: The null hypothesis \( \mu_K=\mu_D \) suggests that the mean listening times for Kendrick and Drake are equal. If the bootstrap distribution is centered around zero, it supports the null hypothesis.

title: Calculating the Observed Difference
text: Calculate the observed difference in sample means: \( \hat{\delta}_{obs}=\bar{K}-\bar{D} \).

title: Analyzing the Bootstrap Distribution
text: Look at the spread and center of the bootstrap distribution. If it is centered around zero, it suggests that the observed difference could be due to random sampling variability.

title: Conclusion from the Bootstrap Distribution
text: Based on the bootstrap distribution, determine if the observed difference \( \hat{\delta}_{obs} \) is likely under the null hypothesis.
